item.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
item.description:
Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen condemns ‘reckless action from Russia towards Denmark’s military’ A Russian warship has fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter in the Baltic Sea, and Nato fighter jets have shot down a drone over Lithuania, in the latest security incidents on the alliance’s eastern flank linked to Russia’s war against Ukraine. Poland also scrambled fighter jets “due to the activity of Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory”, a day after retrieving a suspected Russian drone adrift in its waters. item.title: US confirms it has weapons in space
item.description:
The US Space Force on Monday confirmed for the first time that Washington has weapons deployed in orbit, as the United States, China and Russia expand their military capabilities in space. The disclosure highlights a growing focus on controlling the space domain and protecting satellites vital to military communications, surveillance and navigation.

Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, France 24, The New York Times

item.title: US scraps greenhouse gas rules for power plants
item.description:
The EPA announced it is repealing rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from coal and gas-fired power plants. The move eliminates requirements that would have forced some power plants to sharply reduce their emissions, including through technologies such as carbon capture and storage. Geoff Bennett discussed what this rollback means with Vickie Patton of the Environmental Defense Fund.

Covered by 1 corporate, 1 nonprofit, 2 public.
Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, NBC News, PBS NewsHour

item.title: China tightens travel rules over tech security
item.description:
Chinese authorities imposed new restrictions on foreign travel in order to stop cutting-edge technology and top-flight researchers from leaving, taking a step closer to a regime that had characterized a more closed-off China of decades past. Though senior civil servants and executives at state-owned enterprises have long faced limits on their international travel, the latest rules — announced in July to target export-control and tech-sales violations — apply to a broader swathe of private citizens and lower-level officials working in sensitive areas; those who break the rules face exit bans. “Beyond restricting movement, this approach helps keep both people and capital more firmly within the party-state’s sphere of control ,” one leading expert told the Financial Times. — Prashant Rao

Covered by 1 billionaire/family, 2 public.
Sources: BBC News, Deutsche Welle, Semafor

item.title: Africa's richest man launches continent's biggest share sale
item.description:
Public offering of Aliko Dangote’s Nigerian oil refinery business could swell his net wealth by two-thirds The fortune of Africa’s richest person could swell by two thirds to nearly $60bn (£44bn) after his refinery in Nigeria listed publicly in the continent’s biggest-ever initial public offering. If Monday’s flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals on the Nigerian exchange goes to plan, then Aliko Dangote will add a further $23bn (£17bn) to his $35bn net worth. item.title: Why is pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil suing Columbia University?
item.description:
The university's "deliberate indifference" led to the doxing of multiple group members and Khalil's detention by immigration agents, according to the civil rights lawsuit filed in federal court in New York City.
